analysis: Three changes examined. (1) ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift head line 106 adds `service.wizard.servingScope = request.scope` in onboardingSettings. This is the only production-path change. It passes the onboarding request's serving scope (the local-only versus pair choice, described in the file's comments for `darkbloom cluster local`) into the live settings. The value comes from a local CLI-built ClusterOnboardingRequest, not from the coordinator or a consumer. No new input parsing, path handling, or privilege change is visible. The base code already ran privateQualificationInputRefusal validation before this point. The definition of `servingScope`, how ClusterService and ClusterOnboardingOperations consume it, and whether a local-only scope reliably keeps the cluster out of public or coordinator routing are outside the supplied evidence. This touches the A-018 serving-availability and TB-011 authorization surface only indirectly, so a follow-up pass should confirm that the scope default and mapping fail closed toward local-only. (2) MemberFixtureServicePart.swift is a test-only fixture. It writes a .health file into the test-supplied directory with .withoutOverwriting, gated on an env var. It is not shipped provider code and carries no production attack surface. (3) PlacementSetupCheck.swift is test-only. It passes a new `publicModels: []` argument to ClusterPairServingGrants.publicTrafficLine. The expected values are unchanged for a record-only case. This implies a production API change elsewhere (a public-declaration gate) that is not in this batch, so the new gating semantics in ClusterPairServingGrants were not reviewed. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied lines. The remaining uncertainty is the unseen consumers of servingScope and publicModels.
